questions.q: What is a key risk of every engineer running terraform apply from their own laptop?
options: Terraform cannot run outside a CI platform
There's no shared record of who ran what and what the plan said, and concurrent applies risk state conflicts
Local applies always fail
It requires a paid HashiCorp license
questions.explain: Applying from individual machines leaves no audit trail and increases the risk of two people applying against the same state at the same time.

questions.q: In the example pipeline, when does the plan job run?
options: On every pull request that touches the infra folder
Once per day on a schedule
Only when manually triggered by an administrator
Only after merging to main
questions.explain: The plan job is configured to run on pull_request events touching infra/**, so reviewers see the plan before approving the change.

questions.q: Why does the apply job only run on the main branch in this pipeline?
options: To reduce the pipeline's monthly cost
Because GitHub Actions cannot run apply on pull requests
So nothing ever applies to real infrastructure without first having been reviewed as a plan on a pull request
Because the aws provider requires it
questions.explain: Gating apply behind a merge to main ensures every change was reviewed as a plan first, matching the review process used for application code.

questions.q: Where should provider credentials like AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET or AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID live for a CI pipeline?
options: In the pull request description
Hardcoded directly in the .tf files
In a plaintext file checked into version control
In the CI platform's encrypted secrets store, never committed to the repository
questions.explain: Credentials belong in the CI platform's encrypted secrets store so they're never exposed in the repository's source code or history.

questions.q: What does terraform fmt -check accomplish in the pipeline?
options: It deletes unused resources
It checks cloud provider billing
It automatically applies infrastructure changes
It fails the pipeline if any file isn't formatted to Terraform's canonical style
questions.explain: terraform fmt -check verifies formatting without modifying files, causing the pipeline step to fail if anything is out of the canonical style.
